summary: Session 96 fresh audit merged seven live-code-verified findings into the exhausted Session 95 ledger: match leave retains match-owned workers/render/input resources; multi-tab enforcement fabricates surveillance claims and leaks bound listeners; certified feedback lacks causal signal; an unauthenticated browser-authored remote micro-hint consumes provider capacity despite a deterministic local coach; progression debrief is not rematch-generation-safe; active Doctrine identity disappears at the progression seam; and account recovery uses blocking alerts without pending state. No balance, launch, revenue, or human-retention claim is inferred.

items.title: Replace fabricated surveillance theater with a truthful local tab-collision receipt
items.why: MultiTabModal generates a fake IP and fake fingerprint, labels the state RECORDING and Reported TRUE, and threatens suspension although MultiTabDetector only observes a same-origin localStorage lock. stopMonitoring removes different bound function objects, so its listeners survive teardown; repeated show calls can also stack countdown intervals.

items.title: Retire the unauthenticated browser-authored remote micro-coach path
items.why: CoachHintEngine already renders an immediate deterministic local tactical hint, but an opt-in calls GET /api/vaultfront/micro-hint with browser-authored gold/sites. The provider route has no actor admission, no certified match evidence, no server cache, and is absent from the remote-reservation ordering contract, while every accepted call consumes metered provider capacity.

items.title: Make progression debrief repeatable and generation-safe across rematches
items.why: ProgressionDebrief is a singleton Layer whose requested flag never resets when createRenderer binds a new game. Its polling checks cancelled only before fetch, clears a wait timer without resolving the pending promise, and can apply a prior games receipt after a new match begins. The first post-match debrief can therefore suppress or overwrite later rematch progression.
items.recipe: Bind the component through an explicit game-generation reset, abort/resolve every wait and fetch boundary, reject receipts after generation change, reset claim/loading/certification state, and add consecutive-match plus stale-response tests. Core-loop step: match result → certified reward debrief → chosen rematch goal → next-match progression.

L1.recipe: Reset requested when a new game binds.

L2.recipe: Guard delayed receipts with a game generation.

L3.recipe: Add abortable polling, full state reset, consecutive-rematch tests, and lifecycle integration.

executionLog: Session 96: progression singleton resets per game generation, resolves cancelled waits, rejects stale receipts, and repeats across rematches; consecutive-bind and lifecycle coverage pass.

items.title: Replace blocking account-recovery alerts with bounded accessible state
items.why: AccountModal magic-link recovery uses three window.alert calls, has no pending guard, and leaves the button active during the request. Keyboard and screen-reader users lose modal context, rapid activation can duplicate requests, and success/error truth is detached from the themed account surface.
items.recipe: Add semantic inline validation, pending, success, and retry states with aria-live/role alert, disable duplicate submission, preserve the entered address, reset request state on a new modal session, and cover success/failure/rapid-click/keyboard behavior plus all-theme desktop/mobile rendering. Core-loop step: identity input → trusted account gateway → recovery confirmation reward → return-to-play progression.

L1.recipe: Replace alert with inline status.

L2.recipe: Add pending and duplicate-submit protection.

L3.recipe: Ship accessible state-machine tests, modal-session reset, and rendered theme/mobile proof.

executionLog: Session 96: blocking recovery alerts replaced by inline validation/pending/success/error state with duplicate-submit guard and ARIA relationships; focused tests and desktop/mobile all-theme proof pass.
